area_overview: SQL Server security hierarchy and permission model: server login vs database user, authentication vs authorization, fixed server/database roles, custom database roles, GRANT, and role membership.
key_ideas: A login is server-level identity/authentication; a user is database-level identity/authorization.
A login can be mapped to a database user.
Fixed server roles are server-wide; fixed database roles are scoped to a database.
Custom database roles group permissions for application-specific access.
ALTER ROLE ... ADD MEMBER adds a user to a role.
GRANT gives permissions such as SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/EXECUTE to users or roles.
Security should be read as a hierarchy: server login -> database user -> role membership -> object permissions.

reading_quality.visual_reading: Security screenshots form a compact right-side road. The login/user/roles distinction is readable.
limitations: Some role/permission code snippets are compressed; transcript preserves the hierarchy and common commands.
